sources.quote: Google also folded its Guaranteed and Screened badges into a single Verified badge in late 2025
sources.title: About Google Verified badge - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: Local Services Ads will be simplifying badging by launching a single, more cohesive Google Verified badge for all advertisers effective October 20, 2025. Google will discontinue all existing Local Services Ads badges, including Google Guaranteed, Google Screened, and License Verified by Google, effective October 20, 2025.

sources.quote: include house cleaning among the eligible Canadian categories, and charge per lead instead of per click
sources.title: Business screening and verification requirements - Canada - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: House cleaning professionals perform standard or deep cleans on offices or homes, among other services. Businesses seeking to advertise with Local Services Ads are required to complete appropriate background checks and have appropriate licenses and insurance, as applicable. Background checks are required for select users in the US and Canada.

sources.quote: Bill C-15 narrowed that business-level provision in March 2026, dropping the internationally recognized methodology wording
sources.title: Environmental claims and the Competition Act
sources.evidence: On March 26, 2026, the Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 received Royal Assent, introducing changes to the Competition Act related to environmental claims. These changes removed the requirement for environmental claims to be supported by an internationally recognized methodology.

sources.quote: Bill C-59 added provisions in June 2024 requiring product claims such as
sources.title: Guide to the June 2024 amendments to the Competition Act
sources.evidence: Important amendments to the Competition Act became law on June 20, 2024, following Royal Assent of Bill C-59. Bill C-59 introduced new paragraphs 74.01(1)(b.1) and 74.01(1)(b.2), which require an adequate and proper test to support each environmental representation promoting a product.

sources.quote: keep disinfection claims to products carrying a Health Canada drug identification number
sources.title: Guidance documents on disinfectants: Summary - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Surface disinfectants must have a drug identification number (DIN) before they can be sold in Canada. To receive a DIN and market authorization, applicants must provide safety, efficacy and quality evidence that the product performs as indicated by the label.

sources.title: Guidelines for representing your business on Google - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: Your name should reflect your business's real-world name, as used consistently on your storefront, website, stationery, and as known to customers. Including unnecessary information in your business name isn't permitted, and could result in the suspension of your Business Profile.

sources.quote: a solicitation can require cleaners in federal buildings to hold Reliability Status screening
sources.title: Security requirements for contracting with the Government of Canada - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Contractor/offeror personnel requiring access to sensitive work site(s) must each hold a valid reliability status, granted or approved by the CSP, PWGSC. The Contract Security Program (CSP) provides security screening of organizations and their personnel for solicitations and contracts with security requirements.

sources.quote: falls under a provincial decree administered by the comités paritaires de l'entretien d'édifices publics, which sets minimum working conditions for that workforce
sources.publisher: Comité paritaire de l'entretien d'édifices publics, région de Montréal
sources.title: Le décret - Comité paritaire de l'entretien d'édifices publics, région de Montréal
sources.evidence: Le Comité paritaire de l'entretien d'édifices publics est un organisme mandaté par le Gouvernement du Québec pour assurer l'application du Décret par l'ensemble de l'industrie d'entretien d'édifices publics dans la grande région de Montréal. Le décret détermine pour ce secteur des conditions de travail minimales supérieures aux normes minimales du travail, entre autres le salaire, les vacances, les congés fériés, les congés de maladie et le régime de retraite collectif.

flags.quote: which makes worker classification under CRA guide RC4110 a marketing question as much as a payroll one
flags.issue: The CRA guide RC4110 (Employee or Self-employed) was cancelled as of January 30, 2026 and replaced with the web guidance titled Employment status: Employee or self-employed; the reference to RC4110 as a current guide is outdated.
